_meta.status: Oct 28 hemorrhage set from OCT28_MEDICAL_ANSWERS section 4. Textbook anchors (ATLS / TCCC / NREMT / PHTLS). Needs sign-off from a certified medic before Nov 4.
generalRules: Every intervention can loosen or fail after patient movement (log roll, cot transfer, loading). A reassessment check is required after each move.
Every hand on the wound is a hand not doing anything else. Direct pressure occupies whoever holds it.

interventions.name: Tourniquet, high and tight (CAT)
interventions.timeCost_s: 20-40 for a trained provider: route strap and pull tight 10-15 s, crank windlass about 3 s per half-turn, lock in clip, write time 5 s
interventions.placement: As high on the thigh as possible, groin crease. Once past the immediate threat, can move to 2-3 in above the wound, on skin. Fixed when bleeding stops AND distal pulse is gone.
failureModes: slack_strap: strap slack before cranking, windlass maxes out without occluding, player must start over
venous_tourniquet: too loose, blocks venous return but not arterial inflow, bleed rate x1.3, limb engorged and blue
over_knee_joint: ineffective, x0.9 of the original bleed
late: blood loss keeps accruing at full rate until it is on
no_time_written: logged, missing from MIST
single_cat_large_thigh_failure_TUNE: 25 percent chance one CAT cannot fully occlude, 10-20 percent residual flow, trigger for second tourniquet
sideEffects: Pain +3. Patient begs you to loosen it.
Over 6 h: limb likely lost (outcome projection).
interventions.notes: Thigh: about 3 half-turns to occlude if the strap was pulled tight first, TUNE.

interventions.name: Second tourniquet, proximal to first
interventions.placement: Directly above (proximal to) the first, side by side, not overlapping. Combined, they bring the bleed to 0.
failureModes: below_first_or_over_wound: no effect
loosened_first_to_place_second: full bleed resumes during the gap
overlapping_windlasses: neither locks properly, partial effect, x0.5 residual
interventions.notes: Trigger is the 25 percent single-CAT failure on a large thigh (TUNE).

interventions.name: Hemostatic packing + 3 min pressure (Combat Gauze / QuikClot)
interventions.timeCost_s: Packing 30-90 s by wound size (about 60 s for thigh-size), then 3 min continuous firm pressure, then a pressure dressing over it
interventions.use: Junctional wounds (groin, axilla) or any wound a tourniquet cannot reach. Also an adjunct before converting a tourniquet.
interventions.technique: Gauze packed INTO the wound, onto the bleeding source, until the wound is full. With 3 min of pressure the arterial bleed drops by about 90 percent, and the dressing holds that.
failureModes: gauze_on_top_not_packed: only about 35 percent reduction
pressure_released_before_3min_TUNE: 60 percent rebleed chance
peeking_or_removing_packing: disrupts the clot, bleed restarts at full rate, player must repack
plain_gauze_instead_of_hemostatic: about 75 percent reduction instead of 90
junctional_arterial_packing_alone_TUNE: about 80 percent success rate, on failure a junctional tourniquet is needed
interventions.notes: IDs hemostatic_packing_firm_3min_pressure and hemostatic_packing_if_not_tourniquetable in trauma_library.json both resolve to this entry.

interventions.name: Direct pressure
interventions.timeCost_s: Starts within 2-5 s. Must be held continuously, ties up a provider (delegate to partner or bystander).
interventions.technique: Venous or minor bleeds controlled at about 85-95 percent. Femoral arterial: firm pressure (heel of hand or knee, bodyweight) gives about 50-60 percent reduction. A bridge, not a fix.
failureModes: light_pressure: about 20 percent
not_over_source: about 10 percent
lifting_to_look: full rate resumes instantly
fatigue_TUNE: about -5 percent effectiveness per minute after 3 min unless someone swaps in
patient_moved: pressure is lost until re-established
interventions.notes: Bystander shirt at scene start counts as direct pressure at about 50 percent until the player takes over.

interventions.name: Pressure dressing (Israeli / emergency trauma bandage)
interventions.technique: Holds pressure over packing (maintains about 90 percent of the packing effect) or controls venous and minor bleeds. Over an unpacked femoral arterial wound, only about 40 percent reduction.
failureModes: too_loose: soaks through, about 15 percent effect
too_tight: becomes a distal venous tourniquet, distal cap refill goes long and limb swells, PMS check catches it
soaked_through: correct move is escalate to tourniquet or pack; adding more layers on top is acceptable for venous bleeds
removing_soaked_dressing: restarts the bleed
interventions.notes: Escalate, do not stack, on arterial soak-through.
